title: Global and regional amyloid-β in explaining APOE-ε4 and sex associations with medial temporal tau: a neuropathology study
title_zh: 全局与区域性淀粉样蛋白β在解释APOE-ε4与性别与内侧颞叶tau关联中的作用：一项神经病理学研究
abstract: Abstract The medial temporal lobe (MTL) is a key region in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathogenesis, affected early by tau pathology. While female sex and APOE-ε4 are two known risk factors that affect tau levels, whether these factors drive tau in the MTL via amyloid-dependent or amyloid-independent mechanisms remains unclear. We investigated these relationships in two large neuropathological cohorts comprising 2550 participants from the Religious Orders Study/Memory and Aging Project (ROS/MAP; n =1587, main cohort) and Arizona Study of Aging and Neurodegenerative Disorders (AZSAND; n=963, replication cohort) covering the whole AD continuum. Neuropathological assessments of global neocortical and regional MTL amyloid-β burden were used to determine the extent to which amyloid-β pathology mediated associations of APOE-ε4 carriership and sex with MTL tau burden. In both cohorts, APOE-ε4 carriership and female sex were associated with significantly greater MTL tau pathology (all p <0.001). Adjustment for global amyloid-β attenuated but did not eliminate these associations ( p ≤0.024). However, after jointly accounting for global and MTL amyloid-β burden, the association between APOE-ε4 and MTL tau was no longer significant in either cohort ( p ≥0.19), whereas the association between female sex and MTL tau remained robust ( p ≤0.004). Models incorporating both global and regional MTL amyloid-β explained substantially more variance in MTL tau burden than models including only global amyloid-β, and results were replicated when further adjusting for diagnostic group or neocortical tau burden. These findings suggest that APOE-ε4 and female sex influence MTL tau accumulation through partially distinct pathogenic pathways, supporting an additional contribution of regional amyloid-β to the APOE-ε4-associated MTL tau burden while implicating additional amyloid-independent mechanisms in female vulnerability to tau accumulation.
abstract_zh: 摘要 内侧颞叶（MTL）是阿尔茨海默病（AD）发病机制中的关键区域，早期受tau病理影响。女性性别和APOE-ε4是已知的两种影响tau水平的风险因素，但这些因素是否通过淀粉样蛋白依赖或非依赖机制驱动MTL中的tau仍不清楚。我们在两大神经病理学队列中研究了这些关系，样本共2550名参与者，来自宗教团体研究/记忆与衰老项目（ROS/MAP；n=1587，主队列）和亚利桑那州老龄化与神经退行性疾病研究（AZSAND；n=963，复制队列），覆盖整个AD连续体。使用全局新皮质和区域性MTL淀粉样蛋白β负荷的神经病理学评估，确定淀粉样蛋白β病理在APOE-ε4携带与性别与MTL tau负荷关联中的中介程度。在两队列中，APOE-ε4携带与女性性别均与显著更高的MTL tau病理相关（均p<0.001）。调整全局淀粉样蛋白β后，这些关联被削弱但未消除（p≤0.024）。然而，在同时考虑全局和MTL淀粉样蛋白β负荷后，APOE-ε4与MTL tau的关联在任何队列中均不显著（p≥0.19），而女性性别与MTL tau的关联仍保持稳健（p≤0.004）。同时纳入全局和区域性MTL淀粉样蛋白β的模型比仅包含全局淀粉样蛋白β的模型解释了更多MTL tau负荷的方差，且在进一步调整诊断组或新皮质tau负荷后结果仍被复制。这些发现表明APOE-ε4和女性性别通过部分不同的致病通路影响MTL tau积累，支持区域性淀粉样蛋白β对APOE-ε4相关MTL tau负荷的额外贡献，同时提示女性对tau积累的易感性涉及额外的非淀粉样蛋白机制。
